Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that is it from this game and hosts India have taken a 2-0 lead in the five-match T20I series and can seal the series in the next game. England on the other hand will be much more confident with how they played in this game and would want to get the next win and make the series interesting. The 3rd T20I will be played in Rajkot on Tuesday, the 28th of January and will begin at 7 pm IST (1.30 pm GMT) but you can join us an hour in advance for the build-up as well. Till then, take care and goodbye!

Tilak Varma is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his match-winning knock. Varma starts by saying that the wicket was slightly two-paced and wickets were falling at the other end but remembered what the coach told him and he tried to play according to the situation. Adds that the team has decided that the left-hand right-hand combination is the way to go at the top in order to keep the bowlers guessing. Mentions that he faced very quick pacers in South Africa where the ball was coming on much quicker and that's why he was able to play the English pacers. Ends by applauding Ravi Bishnoi and the two crucial boundaries he hit.

Suryakumar Yadav, the skipper of India says England bowled very well and is happy to have gotten over the line. Adds that they have been playing with an extra batter for the past few series which gives them a good cushion and allows some aggressive brand of cricket but also mentions how the team adapts to situations like in this game. Appreciates Tilak Varma's knock and also says Ravi Bishnoi puts a lot of effort during the practice and wants to contribute with both bat and ball. Lauds Arshadeep Singh as well. States that the atmosphere in the dugout is very calm and they will keep trying to play this brand of cricket.

Jos Buttler, the captain of England says that it was a great game and it was an exciting ending and gives credit to Tilak for getting India over the line. Adds that it was good to push India and reckons that they did well to end to a nearly defendable score. Mentions that there were a lot of positives and goes on to mention debutant Jamie Smith and Brydon Carse for the way they played. Adds that the Indian spinners are always going to take wickets which he doesn't mind as long as they are getting hit as well.
The presentation ceremony...

Earlier in the game, Suryakumar Yadav put England into bat first and just like the first T20I, it was Arshdeep Singh who git rid of Phil Salt with a short delivery early on. And just like the previous game, it was Jos Buttler who looked England's best batter and played some eye-catching shots. The Indian spinners did make a mark in the innings as well and Varun Chakravarthy picked up a couple of big wickets and so did Axar Patel. As for England debutant Jamie Smith showed good promise and so did Brydon Carse who then got run out at a crucial juncture as England huffed and puffed to 165 runs. In reply, we got a cliffhanger of a game but it was Tilak Varma and his calm head that was the difference between the two teams.

Ravi Bishnoi is down for a quick chat. He says when he went out to bat they decided to keep things simple and not take any unnecessary risks. Mentions that with a slip in place, he knew Livingstone would look to try and get him out so he took the chance and found the boundary. Appreciates the way Tilak batted and says he is consistently performing well and is up to something big going ahead.

England will be disappointed in the end and will think that they had this one in the bag more than once in that run chase. Jofra Archer and Mark Wood bowled a fiery spell up top and picked up a couple of wickets but Archer leaked a few too many boundaries and it was then the likes of Brydon Carse and Adil Rashid who stepped up in the middle overs and got England into a position of promise. Rashid dropped Sundar's catch as well which did cost England about 15 or so runs and then Archer's final over went for plenty, putting the visitors on the back foot again. They fought well and took it deep but just couldn't get rid of Varma nor could they stop the tailenders from getting those streaky boundaries and will now have to win 3 on the bounce to seal a comeback series win.

Needing 166 runs for victory, India got out of the blocks quickly again but their openers were undone by some serious pace bowling. Tilak Varma though kept the ante up in the Powerplay and even Suryakumar Yadav got a few boundaries away before getting out. India though were pegged back soon as they went from 58/2 to 78/5 and needed a partnership of some sorts. It was the local boy, Washington Sundar who lended a hand to Varma and the pair got the hosts back in front before the tables turned yet again. India lost wickets in a heap but Varma kept his cool and thanks to a few boundaries got away by Arshdeep Singh and then Ravi Bishnoi, Varma managed to steer his side over the line.

What a finish to the game and Tilak Varma blasts off in celebration and rightly so. The game ebbed and flowed one way then the other but in the end, it is India who have managed to get over the line right at the death and take a 2-0 lead in the five-match T20I series. But spare a thought for England, they made a match out of this one and were even ahead at one stage but simply couldn't hang on.

FOUR! Tilak Varma takes India home! Jamie Overton lands it full and on off, Tilak Varma crunches his drive through covers and finds the fence. Takes off for a celebratory sprint and acknowledges the cheer from the crowd and his team. With this 2 wickets victory, India take a 2-0 lead in the series.

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.2: Adil Rashid to Tilak Varma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Rashid comes into the attack and starts with a full one, on off, Dhruv Jurel eases it to deep cover for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Adil Rashid to Dhruv Jurel, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length, angling away, outside off, Tilak Varma looks to slash at it but is beaten by the pace. India end the Powerplay at 59/3!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Brydon Carse to Tilak Varma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length, on middle, Jurel pulls it to deep square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Brydon Carse to Dhruv Jurel, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Dhruv Jurel is the new batter in.

OUT! PLAYED'ON! Brydon Carse gets a wicket in his very first over and England are back in it. Hits the hard length, around off, coming in with the angle at good pace. Suryakumar Yadav hops to drop it down the deck but gets and inside edge that drops down and skids through to rattle into the stumps.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Brydon Carse to Suryakumar Yadav, OUT! b Brydon Carse.

Commentary.Commentary: Keeps it tight on a length, on off, Varma taps it to mid off and takes a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Brydon Carse to Tilak Varma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Angling away, very full and outside off, Tilak Varma looks to reach for it but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Brydon Carse to Tilak Varma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Carse is greeted into the attack with a six! HE bangs it short and on middle and leg, right at the head, Tilak Varma swivels a bit and pulls it from very close to his body and gets the ball sailing behind short third for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Brydon Carse to Tilak Varma, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Beaten! Bowled on a hard length and outside off with a hint of away movement on it. SKY backs away and gets low to angle it over short third but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Jofra Archer to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length, angled into the batter, Tilak Varma gives the charge but picks the slower one and just holds his shape before pushing it away into the off side for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Jofra Archer to Tilak Varma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Top edge but Archer's pace has taken that one over the ropes and into the sightscreen. Just under 145 kph, banged in well short and just down leg, Tilak Varma gets inside the line to pull but gets hurried and gets a top edge right back over the keeper's head for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Jofra Archer to Tilak Varma, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Around the wicket now and nails it into the blockhole on off, Varma blocks it out to covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Jofra Archer to Tilak Varma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Wow, that is some shot from Tilak Varma. Archer goes full now and bowls it around off at over 150 clicks, Varma threatens to get across but stays put and just flicks it up and over deep backward square leg for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Jofra Archer to Tilak Varma, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Crashed through the off side! A hard-length delivery at 147 clicks, around the top of off, Varma is quick to back away and stays low before slashing it away past point for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Jofra Archer to Tilak Varma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Takes pace off now and bowls it back of a length and outside off, Suryakumar Yadav looks to guide it away off the back foot but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Mark Wood to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Just out of reach and will roll away into the fence! Pitched-up delivery, straying onto the pads at 152.7 kph, SKY looks to pick it up and flick but mistimes it a bit and gets it over square leg for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Mark Wood to Suryakumar Yadav, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Length ball, fuller and pushed wider of the off stump, Varma crouches down and angles it down to deep third for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Mark Wood to Tilak Varma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: A quick bumper now from Wood, at 148 clicks and banged in over middle, Tilak Varma looks to hook it away but is beaten all ends up.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Mark Wood to Tilak Varma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Keeps the pace right up and bowls it back of a length, getting the ball to jump off the deck, Varma hops back and manages to keep it down.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Mark Wood to Tilak Varma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a hard length in the channel outside off, and darting across the left-hander off the deck, Varma leaves it alone.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Mark Wood to Tilak Varma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Good length, angling down leg, Tilak Varma looks to get inside the line and scoop but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Mark Wood to Tilak Varma, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Geez, that's quick! A proper bumper this, dug in quick and short outside off, Suryakumar Yadav tries to uppercut but can't lay bat on it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Jofra Archer to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Pace off again, bowled a fraction short and outside off, Suryakumar Yadav hangs back and cuts it quickly and wide of short third for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Jofra Archer to Suryakumar Yadav, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Attempted slower ball, bowled full and spilled down the leg side for a wide.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Jofra Archer to Suryakumar Yadav, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! That's rocketed to the fence! A bit short and wide, Suryakumar Yadav stays put and just throws his hands at it, cutting it firmly in front of point for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Jofra Archer to Suryakumar Yadav, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: OUT! CAUGHT! Both Indian openers back in the hut and the English pacers have their tails up! Jofra Archer with another quick bumper, bowling it at 148 clicks and at a difficult height over middle and leg. Sanju Samson looks to hang back and take on the pull but is late on it and the ball goes off the sticker of the bat and high towards deep mid-wicket. Brydon Carse was just stationed out there for this shot and Samson has suckered into playing it straight to him. Carse holds on and Archer gets his man. Also, Suryakumar Yadav is the new batter in.
Commentary.Howout: c Brydon Carse b Jofra Archer
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Jofra Archer to Sanju Samson, OUT! c Brydon Carse b Jofra Archer.

Commentary.Commentary: Just over the infield! Short of a length and angled into the rib cage at 148.5 clicks, Samson looks to go hard at the pull but is hurried and mistimes it just over mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Jofra Archer to Sanju Samson, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Sanju Samson is early to back away and Archer follows him with a quick bumper. Sanju gets hurried while looking to pull and gets a top edge right into the body.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Jofra Archer to Sanju Samson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: This is bowled fuller and on leg stump, Tilak Varma nudges it out on the leg side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Mark Wood to Tilak Varma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Wood falls over again on the followthrough but hits the mark with his line and length. Quick and on a good length around the top of off, Samson pats it down wide of mid on for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Mark Wood to Sanju Samson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard-length delivery, angling back into the pads, Varma tucks it away neatly behind square leg and picks up a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Mark Wood to Tilak Varma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Tilak Varma walks in at number 3 for India.

OUT! LBW! Oh, that's jagged back in quickly and the umpire's finger goes up. Mark Wood steams in and bangs it in on a hard length on middle at over 147 clicks and falls over as the ball seams back in off the deck. Abhishek Sharma stays put looking to pull but is too quick and he is undone by the pace. Sharma has a chat with Samson and takes the review. Clearly no bat involved and Ball Tracking shows that the ball actually would have held its line and would have crashed into middle stump. England see the back of the aggressive Abhishek Sharma early on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Mark Wood to Abhishek Sharma, OUT! lbw b Mark Wood.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Pitched up on leg and swinging down the leg side, Sharma gets across to flick but misses and a wide is called.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Mark Wood to Abhishek Sharma, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length in the channel outside off, seaming away a touch, Samson guides it down to deep third for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Mark Wood to Sanju Samson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, that is prodigious movement! Wood bangs it in on a shortish length around off and gets it to seam away. Sanju Samson reluctantly looks to pull and is well beaten.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Mark Wood to Sanju Samson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: It will be Mark Wood to share the attack from the other end.

FOUR! Up and over! Shorter in length again and outside off, at over 149 clicks, the deep third fielder was just brought in and Sharma gets across to flail it away exactly in that area for another boundary. India 13/0 after the first over of the chase!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Jofra Archer to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Oh, that's aggressive from Abhishek Sharma. Archer clocks in at 146 KPH and angles it in on a good length, Sharma just backs away and gives the charge before hammering it over extra cover for another boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Jofra Archer to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: That's banged in quick and short outside off, zipping through off the deck, Abhishek Sharma looks to go after it but is well beaten.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Jofra Archer to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Just timed beautifully. Short of a good length and outside off at almost 147 clicks, Sharma just presses back and punches it up and over covers for a boundary to get off the mark.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Jofra Archer to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Too hot to handle! Around the wicket to the left-hander, bowled back of a length and outside off, seaming away at searing pace, Abhishek Sharma stands tall to hammer it through covers but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Jofra Archer to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Gets a good hand on it! Archer steams in from over the wicket and digs it in short right away, at the front shoulder. Sanju Samson mistimes the pull to the left of square leg where the fielder dives across and makes a half stop. The batters get a single and Samson is off the mark.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Jofra Archer to Sanju Samson, 1 run.
